conf.description: PostgreSQL Audit (pgaudit) / pgaudit dataset / syslog-raw: strips the operator log_line_prefix (assumed %m [%p] %u@%d %c) to recover timestamp/pid/user/database/session-id, then splits the AUDIT: CSV tail (config-dependent column count) with a second regex_extract; no Elastic integration or pack understands pgAudit's AUDIT body.

conf.comment: postgresql-audit / pgaudit / syslog-raw. pgAudit rides the ordinary server log, so an audit line is <log_line_prefix><AUDIT: CSV tail>. No Elastic integration or Cribl Pack has pgAudit awareness (integration grok stops at the LOG token; no Packs installed), so this is a hand-built parser. ASSUMES log_line_prefix = '%m [%p] %u@%d %c ' per the map's documented escapes (%m,%p,%u,%d,%c) - the literal prefix is operator-configured and unverifiable from the map alone; say so in README. Multi-line reassembly of STATEMENT (which can contain literal newlines) is expected to happen at the Source event breaker before this pipeline runs - out of scope for a pipeline object. Order: parse -> compute event.type/event.action/_time from ORIGINAL field names -> batched rename -> event.dataset, per the compute-before-rename rule.

functions.description: why this is a hand-built parser and what the prefix format assumes
strip log_line_prefix, recover timestamp/pid/user/database/session id, isolate the AUDIT CSV tail
split the AUDIT tail; ROWS group is optional because pgaudit.log_rows changes the column count
derive event.type/event.action/_time from the ORIGINAL parsed field names, before rename nests them
batch rename every clean-named parsed field to its ECS or custom postgresql.pgaudit.* target
tag the dataset (no hyphen, per Elastic data-stream naming) and drop intermediate/consumed fields
